purpose:
Most bus services are provided commercially,
but the Council can supplement these services with additional local
bus services to increase accessibility and sustainable transport in
the council area.

 

The Council has its own supported
bus service budget of £283,000 and this is currently
supplemented by funding from Section 106 developer contributions
and Department for Transport grants.

 

The North Northamptonshire Bus
Service Improvement Plan (BSIP) outlines ambitions to increase
patronage for local bus services which is most likely to be
achieved by uplifting capacity in urban areas. The Council received
BSIP funding in three tranches to help achieve this aim with DfT
agreeing this could fund services to March 2026.

The Executive on
14th
September 2023 delegated authority
to the Executive Member for Highways, Travel & Assets in
consultation with the Executive Director of Place & Economy to
take any actions needed to award the local bus service contracts
and any further decisions/actions relating to expenditure of the
BSIP+ funding.

 

As reported to Executive on 18
April 2024, a series of service improvements has been developed for
implementation using this funding, subject to affordability and
value for money.  Annex 5 provides a status update for the
service improvements reported to Executive.

 

The new/improved services are
being introduced on a phased basis. Because of the uncertainty of
future grant funding levels, many contracts have been awarded with
initial terms ending on 29th
March 2025, with possible
extensions for one or more further years. 

 

The allocation of further revenue
grant funding to support bus services makes it affordable to extend
all the contracts currently expiring on 28th
March 2026 on which extensions are
exercisable for a further year to 27th
March 2027.

 

However, contract DMN408 for one
evening journey on Corby service 2C will not be extended beyond the
current contract termination on 28th
March 2026 as this service
represents poor value for money, carrying no more than one
passenger per journey.

One of the schemes agreed for 2025/26 funding

school street at St Barnabas Street,

Northamptonshire and the boundaries of the former boroughs and
districts which still reference former

Decision
Title



Licence between Northamptonshire
Council and Heidelberg (Hanson Quarry Products
Europe) to enable the safe
replacement of NNC Ref. 3122 – White Mills Bridge.





Date of
decision (same as date form signed)



01/12/2025





Key
Decision



No





Decision

 



Grant a Licence to allow North
Northamptonshire Council to use the land owned by Heidelberg
(Hanson
Quarry Products Europe).





Reason/s for
Decision



Kier Transportation Ltd working on
behalf of North Northamptonshire Council have requested the use of
the Heidelberg (Hanson Quarry Products
Europe) adjacent to Station
Road, Earls Barton. The land comprises concrete entrance, lockable
and a solid concrete slab area, suitable for car parking and
compound/material storage throughout the duration of the
replacement of NNC Ref. 3122 - White Mills Bridge.





Alternative
options considered and rejected



Due to the limited working width
of the site, it is not possible to safely situate the compound,
welfare, storage and office facilities within the highway boundary,
therefore the land adjacent to the North-East corner of the bridge
is nearest suitable site compound. The are to the south of the
bridge is prone to flooding and therefore unsuitable for plant
machinery/traffic.





Legal
implications



New Licence required





Financial
implications



Licence fee





Other
implications



None known

papers considered

Consultation



To date, stakeholder engagement
has involved Kier Transportation Ltd, North Northamptonshire
Council, Environment Agency, Natural England, Landowners and Local
Businesses. A Kier Transportation Ltd Stakeholder Officer is
assigned to the project to assist with communications.

decision_maker: Executive Member - Planning and Economic Growth
purpose:
1.1.          
To ensure the Council continues to
produce robust and reliable justification in support of Section 106
requirements, it is necessary to regularly review and update the
current evidence base and benchmark costs. This Technical Update
ensures that:

•        
Pupil Yield data from new housing
development is based on latest available figures provided by the
Department for Education

•        
Costs per Pupil Place are based on
latest available benchmarks issued by the Department for Education
and EBDOG (the Education Building Officers Development Group
– a national forum of local authority professionals with
responsibility for school place delivery)

•        
Benchmark costs for Library
infrastructure are based on latest available figures issued by the
Royal Institute of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) for public library
construction projects.

 

1.2.          
To ensure the Council is able to
secure sufficient S106 developer contributions to support the
delivery of new and expanded Education and Library infrastructure,
to meet the needs arising from new housing development.

 

1.3.          
To allow the Council to operate in
a fair and transparent way, by providing certainty and parity for
developers seeking to operate within North
Northamptonshire

 

1.4.          
To provide certainty for local
communities that additional development coming forward in their
area will be accompanied by appropriate infrastructure.

 

1.5.          
To avoid any unnecessary delays in
the determination of planning applications and the agreement of
S106 contributions by basing decisions on latest guidance issued by
the relevant national bodies, including the Department for
Education and Arts Council England.
